children: Windward Bio Group AG filed a registration statement for its initial public offering of common shares. The clinical-stage biotechnology company is seeking to list its shares on the Nasdaq Global Market under the proposed ticker WWB. The filing does not yet specify the offering price, share count or proceeds, and the company plans to use net proceeds primarily to advance its clinical programs.

Windward Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing long-acting antibody medicines for respiratory and skin diseases. Its lead candidate, WIN378, targets TSLP and is being studied in asthma and COPD, with the company pursuing a potential twice-yearly dosing schedule. WIN027 is an investigational bispecific antibody designed to target both TSLP and IL-13; it is in Phase 1 testing, with planned studies in COPD and atopic dermatitis. The company also has an earlier-stage bispecific antibody research program.

Windward Bio licenses its lead candidates from biotechnology partners and relies on outside manufacturers and clinical research organizations. It holds rights to develop and commercialize WIN378 outside Greater China and certain Asian markets, and WIN027 outside Greater China. The company says its candidates are designed for less frequent dosing and, in the case of WIN027, simultaneous targeting of two disease pathways; these potential advantages have not yet been established in pivotal trials.
: The company estimates that biologic therapies for asthma, COPD and atopic dermatitis represent a $60 billion peak market opportunity.

: Windward estimates that global sales of severe-asthma biologics were approximately $14 billion in 2025 and projects a $30 billion peak market when combined with COPD biologic treatment; it estimates atopic-dermatitis systemic treatments generated approximately $15 billion in 2025 and could reach $30 billion at peak.

: The company estimates biologic treatment reaches about 20% of eligible severe-asthma patients, 1% of eligible moderate-to-severe COPD patients and 15% of eligible moderate-to-severe atopic-dermatitis patients.
: Companies and programs named in the filing include Amgen, AstraZeneca, GSK, Sanofi, Upstream Bio, Generate Biomedicines and KeyMed/Belenos Bio.
: The company points to growing use of biologics, interest in broader pathway targeting and efforts to improve dosing convenience and treatment adherence.
: Two clinical-stage candidates—WIN378 in Phase 2/3 asthma and Phase 2 COPD studies, and WIN027 in Phase 1—with an additional bispecific program in lead optimization.
: The company expects ten Phase 2 and Phase 3 readouts for WIN378 and WIN027 through 2029, plus four additional readouts from studies conducted by Qyuns.
: 38 employees as of September 30, 2026, including 24 in research and development.
: Employees are based in Switzerland, the United States, the United Kingdom and Spain; clinical development also involves the United States, Australia, China and other international locations.
: WIN378 is licensed from Sichuan Kelun-Biotech and Harbour BioMed; WIN027 is licensed from Qyuns Therapeutics, which also conducts and funds certain China-based studies.
: Not applicable; the company has not generated revenue.
: Operating loss of $44.7 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026.
: Net loss of $42.6 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026; net loss of $48.3 million for 2025.

, Chief Executive Officer and Chair of the Board - Founded Windward Bio and previously led VectivBio through its acquisition by Ironwood Pharmaceuticals; he also co-founded Therachon, acquired by Pfizer.
, Chief Financial Officer - Previously served as CFO of VectivBio and Therachon and held senior finance roles at TiGenix and Cellerix.
, Chief Medical Officer - Previously served as CMO at VectivBio and Voyager Therapeutics and held translational medicine leadership roles at Roche.
, Chief Operating Officer - Previously served as Chief Commercial Officer at VectivBio and held commercial strategy roles at Incyte and Pfizer.
, Chief Legal and Corporate Development Officer - Previously held legal, business and regulatory leadership positions at VectivBio, Trevena and Shire.
: Jefferies, TD Cowen, Piper Sandler and UBS Investment Bank

: Fund development of WIN378 in asthma and COPD, WIN027 in COPD and atopic dermatitis, advance bispecific programs through IND-enabling studies, and support working capital and general corporate purposes.
